# Expectations {#expectations}

In addition to agreeing to follow our communities codes of conduct and the university academic integrity policy, we expect everyone in the group to echo our lab culture (Chapter \@ref(culture)). 

__Individual Development plans:__  Moira will work with each of you to develop your individual development plan that serves to ensure your time in the Decima lab progresses your short, medium, and long-term goals. This is a useful planning document that assists in aligning expectations. Graduate students will revisit the mentoring plan during an individual meeting with Moira at the beginning of each quarter & the start of summer. Other lab members will revisit these at appropriate time scales (e.g. every 6 months).  
A template for these, with thanks to [`@duffy_ma`](https://twitter.com/duffy_ma) can be found [here](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ie3nc6iqW5cWit_MV8BUIVmREbvUZ8b0P9dR8CGgleQ/edit?usp=sharing). 

In addition, it is useful to have broad (for all lab members) and specific (i.e., grad students, research staff, etc.) expectations of our roles clarified. These are outlined below.  


## Email

In the lab, we communicate via email and slack (free version). You should therefore check your email and slack at least once a day during the normal work week. We also make use of Google Docs and issues on GitHub to record institutional knowledge and hold conversations regarding research tasks. Do not expect responses to emails after regular business hours on weekdays, or on weekends. However, because we recognize that lab members should be able to create a working schedule that is right for them, lab members should not be penalized for sending communication during these times.   


## Attendance at regularly scheduled events

Attendance is expected at:

* Departmental seminars  
* Weekly lab meetings  
* Individual meetings with Moira to discuss and work on your research  
* Décima thesis and proposal defenses  

## Outreach

Update for Decima lab and other grant expectations


## Expectations for the PI

Moira (as PI) will (at a minimum) provide:  

* Technical support for analysis (e.g., access to computing, training on techniques)  
* Positive feedback & constructive criticism on work  
* Professional career support  
* Support for non-technical aspects of making career progress  
* Regular meetings to discuss work & maintain progress on goals  
* Provide clear and honest appraisal of your funding situation  


##  Graduate students

You are responsible for your degree. This means you need to stay on top of program and university deadlines, requirements, etc. 

Course of study: Work with Moira when crafting and revisiting your individual mentoring plans to identify classes that you will take during your academic program. Look beyond those offered at SIO to include elsewhere at UCSD, and also at other institutions. A list of classes that lab members have taken, and suggested course of study schedule for Décima lab grad students can be found in Chapter \@ref(courses).  

We schedule regular individual meetings with Moira throughout the year. Meetings are a chance for you to get focused time with Moira to discuss and work on your research. Thus they are your time, not Moira’s. Come with an agenda with a list of things that you want to accomplish and work on during that time, and a list of what was accomplished the previous week.

We share our research at local, national, and international meetings, and publish our findings in the scientific literature. Moira strives to provide financial support for grad students to attend at least one major conference. You should expect to give a presentation (prefereably a talk) on your work at these.

## Undergraduate students

You will most likely be working with one of the lab’s research team as your primary research supervisor. The grad student or postdoc you are working with on your project will be your primary source of contact and you should work with them to establish and define your work schedule, protocols for your work, and to ensure you have the necessary equipment to perform your work tasks.  

Although the grad student / postdoc is your primary contact, always feel like you can reach out to both [Moira](mailto:mdecima@ucsd.edu) as lab PI. We are excited to help you use your position in the lab to further your career goals and want to work with you to help you achieve them.  

UPDATE FOR DECIMA LAB
If you are an hourly worker (either federal work study or grant supported) then it is critical that you complete your timesheets through HR Direct with your hours worked, so that you can get paid. Please submit your electronic timesheet each week by noon on Friday, to allow time for Gavin to approve. Alert your research supervisor AND Gavin as soon as possible if there are any complications with regard to pay. We want you to be compensated for your work in a timely fashion.  


## Postdoctoral researchers

EDIT BELOW FOR DECIMA LAB EXPECTATIONS

In general, postdocs are expected to:  

* Be present and involved in lab meetings, workshops, campus seminars, and conferences.  
* Provide mentorship, technical support, and assistance to other lab members  
* Communicate both successes and sticking points on a regular basis with the PI  
* Work independently and collaboratively  
* Participate in professional development opportunities  
* Lead and assist in designated research projects
